plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value is irrational (you'd lose money if you win), and bidding significantly below your value risks losing to a slightly higher bid, even if it's below your true value. Since it's round 1 and there's no history, I will bid slightly below my value to test the waters.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid your value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value is strictly dominated (you risk overpaying), and any bid below your value might allow someone else to win an item you value more highly. Since we are playing only one round, and given my value is $28, I will bid slightly below that to maximize my chance of winning while minimizing potential loss. I will bid $27.5.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = ~32.67. However, with only one round, a more conservative approach is better. I will bid slightly above my value to discourage others, but not excessively high. I will bid $22.10.
